Postmortem redistribution ratio

Source: R/tox.R
pmrrat.Rd

After death drugs move from organs into the central blood vessels, so that heart blood can read well above the concentration at death. The ratio of the central (heart) to the peripheral (femoral) concentration flags it: at most cut[1] (1) minimal, at most cut[2] (2) modest, above that significant, when the peripheral value is the better guide to the concentration at death.

Usage

pmrrat(cen, per, cut = c(1, 2))

Arguments

cen, per

The central and peripheral blood concentrations: positive numbers, one per case.

cut

The two cut points of the ratio: positive, increasing.

Value

A data frame with one row per case: cen, per, ratio (cen / per) and redist, a factor (minimal, modest, significant).

References

Yarema, M. C. and Becker, C. E. (2005). Key concepts in postmortem drug redistribution. Clinical Toxicology, 43(4), 235-241. doi:10.1081/CLT-58950

Examples

pmrrat(c(0.4, 1.5, 0.9), c(0.5, 1, 0.2))
#>   cen per ratio      redist
#> 1 0.4 0.5   0.8     minimal
#> 2 1.5 1.0   1.5      modest
#> 3 0.9 0.2   4.5 significant
